result.reasoning:
The MECHANISM reproduces exactly as reported, but the "wrong output / corrupts half the history" conclusion does not survive. Three independent reasons, each verified by hand.

(1) The lower-middle value IS this engine's definition of "median", engine-wide. /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/operators/common.py:395-396 defines the house helper as `_median(x) = x.nanmedian(dim=-1).values`, and common.py:456-457 the rolling one as `nanmedian_last(w) = w.nanmedian(dim=-1).values`. Every "median" in the engine routes through those two: built-in `cs_median` (nd_cs.py:134-137), `day_median` (dt_day.py:94-95), `in_median` (dt_in.py:201-202), `in_med` (dt_in.py:384), `ts_median` (nd_ts.py:183), `cross_median` (dt_cross.py:239). Verified by running the engine: `cs_median(torch.tensor([[1.,2.,3.,4.]])) = 2.0`, `common._median(...) = 2.0` — i.e. the reporter's "from-scratch reference" (nanquantile → 2.5) disagrees with AlphaCube's OWN `cs_median`, not the other way round. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:12-13 states outright that its conventions are "the same as AlphaCube's kernels", and the file's two sibling robust-z kernels, `in_madz` (ops_ext.py:392-393) and `cross_madz` (ops_ext.py:654-655), use the identical `torch.nanmedian`. So cs_robust_z at ops_ext.py:445-446 is a line-for-line implementation of its docstring under the only definition of "median" this codebase has. There is no implementation-vs-spec gap.

(2) The daily cross-sectional ORDERING — which is what the selection口径 consumes — is bit-identical under both conventions, because within a day the op is x → (x − m)/(1.4826·MAD + EPS), a strictly increasing affine map with positive slope. Measured on a 1360×4800 panel (6% NaN, 50.7% of days with an even finite count, min 4461 / max 4572 finite stocks): per-day Spearman between the two conventions = 1.000000000000 on every day sampled; with cs_robust_z as the outermost op at halflife 0 the long book is exactly identical (0 holding differences, Sharpe delta 0.00e+00, ann excess identical to all printed digits). Swept S ∈ {4,10,50,200,1000,3000,4200,5000,5400} × both parities: rank changes 0 and top-10% set changes 0 in all 18 cases.

(3) The "qualitative disagreement, not rounding noise" framing is an artifact of the S=4 toy. The gap between the lower middle value and the midpoint is one order-statistic gap, which shrinks like 1/S. On the realistic panel the per-cell difference is: median |dz| = 3.6e-07, mean 3.1e-04, p99 3.8e-03; median RELATIVE |dz|/|z| = 1.3e-07, p99 1.1e-02; pooled Pearson of the two panels 0.99999994. The reporter's "80/180 cells mismatched on even rows" counts how many cells a per-day affine shift touches (by construction: all of them) and says nothing about materiality. After the causal EMA, on both the recorded overlay shape `add(cs_robust_z(a), mul(cs_robust_z(b), 0.5))` and the single-op case, the long-only Sharpe moves by ≤0.03 on levels of 2.2–10.4 (≤0.4% relative, sign random across half-lives) and the annualised excess moves in the 5th decimal (e.g. 0.03934 vs 0.03922).

Honest caveat (does not rescue the finding): in the one amplifying consumer, the recorded `ts_pearson(cs_robust_z(day_last(Close)), 20)` (runs/F111_spearman_qclose/sweep_s3.json : h3_robust_path), the two conventions do diverge — at S≈575 (the largest universe ts_pearson's O(N²) let me fit) per-day Spearman drops to 0.946–0.993 and the book's Sharpe moves by up to 0.34. That is ts_pearson being sensitive to its input's LEVEL, amplifying a definitional choice; it would be ~8× smaller at the real ~4500-stock universe, and it says nothing about which convention is right. Both conventions are deterministic, same-day-only (no look-ahead), and applied identically to train / valid / holdout, so there is no leak and no train-vs-holdout inconsistency either way.

The suggested fix is affirmatively harmful: swapping lines 445-446 to nanquantile would make cs_robust_z the ONLY median in the whole engine that averages the two central values — inconsistent with cs_median / day_median / in_median / ts_median / in_madz / cross_madz — and would silently restate already-recorded numbers (runs/F110_ret_fair_log/sweep_s3.json : h3_ov_cvx_rz, runs/F111_spearman_qclose/sweep_s3.json : h3_robust_path, plus the handoff ledgers), breaking comparability with the user's published tables for zero gain in correctness. (It is at least runnable — nanquantile is actually faster than nanmedian at 1940×9000 = 1.75e7 elements, 0.13s vs 0.23s, and cs_winsor at ops_ext.py:258 already uses it at panel scale — so "it would crash" is not the objection; the objection is that it changes the definition.)
result.reproduction:
Scripts (left in place, read-only w.r.t. the repos): /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/opus_csrobustz/verify.py , verify2.py , verify3.py
Run with: ALPHACUBE_ROOT=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src:/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python verify.py

verify.py A — reporter's toy reproduces verbatim: cs_robust_z([[1,2,3,4]]) = [-0.674490749835968, 0.0, 0.674490749835968, 1.348981499671936]; nanquantile reference = [-1.0117361385324861, -0.33724537951082867, 0.33724537951082867, 1.0117361385324861]. Mechanism confirmed.
verify.py B — but the engine's own median agrees with the kernel, not the reference: common._median([[1,2,3,4]]) = [2.0]; built-in cs_median([[1,2,3,4]]) = 2.0; torch.nanquantile(...,0.5) = [2.5].
verify.py C — S sweep {4,10,50,200,1000,3000,4200,5000,5400} × both parities, 400 heavy-tailed days each: odd-count days match to 0.000e+00 (as reported); even-count days differ in level but "rank chg" = 0 and "top10% set chg" = 0 in EVERY row.
verify.py D / verify2.py — 1360×4800 panel, 6% NaN, even finite count on 50.7% of days. Single-op: median|dz| 3.6e-07, p99 3.8e-03, median relative 1.3e-07, pooled corr 0.99999994, per-day Spearman min 1.000000000000. Long book, cs_robust_z outermost: hl=0 → 0 holding diffs and Sharpe delta exactly 0.00e+00; hl∈{1..20} → |ΔSharpe| ≤ 9.1e-03 on 2.2–8.3, ann excess 0.03934 vs 0.03922.
verify2.py degenerate cases — "2401 flat / 2399 spread (majority tie)" blows up to 2.399e+12 under BOTH conventions, i.e. the one genuinely dangerous day is convention-independent and the suggested fix does not address it.
verify.py E — nanquantile is runnable and fast at panel scale (1940×9000, numel 1.75e7: nanmedian 0.232s vs nanquantile 0.126s), so the fix is not rejected on feasibility.
verify3.py — the amplifying consumer, ts_pearson(cs_robust_z(Close),20) at S≈575: per-day Spearman min 0.9460 / mean 0.9926, |ΔSharpe| up to 0.34. Reported for completeness; this is level-sensitivity of ts_pearson, not evidence that either median convention is wrong.
